- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., post-0.37 sentiment spikes).
- Underestimate downward moves when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.70 or -0.67) — model tends to lag or underreact.
- When sentiment is mildly negative (-0.10 to -0.30), model often overcorrects upward, leading to overshoots in early forecast days.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently overpredicts mid-term highs and underpredicts lows — adjust for 3-5 day smoothing in forecast tails.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid assuming momentum; sentiment decay (e.g., -0.07 to -0.13) should trigger downward bias correction.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to adjust — add a 1-2 day lag correction for sentiment reversal.
